self.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Physical Records
detail.summary: Objective records are defined by the proliferation of information into the environment (redundancy), where independent observers can extract the same data without disturbing the system. We extend this by examining the limits of information availability under scrambling, and the necessity of stable infrastructure for long-distance record accessibility.
detail.reason: This revision incorporates information scrambling dynamics and physical-layer architecture, broadening the scope from purely theoretical Quantum Darwinism to operational considerations for record reliability.

detail.title: Synthesis on Objective Record Formation and Physical Infrastructure
detail.summary: This journal entry updates the institutional research into the objective status of physical records. We synthesize evidence from Quantum Darwinism, information scrambling dynamics, and physical-layer quantum infrastructure. Objective reality emerges from the redundancy of information broadcast into the environment; however, the stability of this information is bounded by scrambling dynamics in the quantum substrate. Scaling these observations to independent observers requires physical infrastructure capable of overcoming decoherence at scale.
